ingredients.name: Pork shoulder or belly
ingredients.notes: cut into 2cm cubes; a mix of fatty and lean pieces gives the best texture

ingredients.name: Vinegar
ingredients.notes: white, apple cider, or coconut vinegar; for the marinade

steps.instruction: Marinate the pork cubes with black pepper, vinegar, 1 tbsp soy sauce, chilli powder, and salt. Mix well and leave for at least 30 minutes, or overnight refrigerated.

Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Fry the marinated pork in batches until golden brown on all sides and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes per batch. Remove and set aside. The pork renders its own fat as it cooks -- some cooks add no additional oil at this stage.
In the same pan with the remaining oil, fry the onion wedges, garlic, ginger, banana peppers, and green chillies over high heat for 2-3 minutes, keeping them slightly crunchy.
Add the curry powder (if using), remaining soy sauce, ketchup, and sugar. Stir to combine into a glossy sauce.
Add the fried pork back into the pan. Add the tomato wedges. Toss everything together over high heat for 2-3 minutes until the pork is well coated in the glossy red-brown sauce.
Taste and adjust sweetness, heat, and salt. Serve immediately with plain rice or bread.

source_site: zestofceylon.wordpress.com, cross-checked against srilankanrecipes.info, keeperofthekitchen.com, cambridgefoodies.me.uk, infolanka.com (Malini's Kitchen), theflavorbender.com (devilled beef), and hrcookery.ca
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 7+ independent sources; strong agreement on the ketchup+soy+vinegar+sugar sauce base shared with all devilled dishes; pork is the same technique as devilled chicken (sl_032) and devilled fish (sl_033)
notes: Devilled pork uses the same core Sri Lankan-Chinese fusion sauce technique as devilled chicken (sl_032) and devilled fish (sl_033) -- ketchup, soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar -- applied to pork. The key difference from chicken is that pork belly or shoulder is fattier and renders its own oil during frying, so less added oil is needed. Some recipes boil the pork first until tender before frying (especially for tougher cuts), then fry and toss in the sauce; this entry uses the direct fry method for boneless shoulder or belly, which are tender enough without pre-boiling. As with all devilled dishes, vegetables should be kept crunchy and the final toss in sauce should be brief -- overcooking the vegetables or the sauce will make the dish soft rather than glossy and sticky.
